text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Wednesday.
- Croatia to regain authority over its last rebel Serb enclave in Eastern Slavonia in April, President Tudjman says in an interview with the main dailies.
- Demographic research shows Croatia has had a negative birth-rate since 1981, but some parameters show 1996 might bring change.
- Introduction of 22 percent VAT in January might be detrimental to Croatian tourism, hoteliers say in a letter sent to President Tudjman demanding reduction.
- Income taxes for farms to be cancelled under proposed new law.

- Croatian banks have 50 percent surplus employees, but not enough experts. Lack of trained managers caused delay in start of some foreign operations, says Dragutin Bohus, representative of Austrian banks.
- Speculative investors caused fast growth of some stocks, but euphoria is damaging for brokers as hard landing must come sooner or later, says Dubravko Zganec, chairman of brokers' association.
- Shipbuilders on ascent in the stock market, as prices of hoteliers edge down.

- Labour is the cheapest Croatian product: average worker earns 3.06 German marks an hour, while an average family makes only 755 marks a month, below 1,200 marks minimum needed for bare survival. Reduced income taxes and a more realistic kuna exchange rate would help improve the situation.
- Jadroplov shipper was last week's biggest gainer on Zagreb bourse, jumping from 150 to 215 kuna. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
